episode: Inside Our Most Dramatic Flip Yet, From Dated to Dream Home in 4 Weeks
assessment: King bought this one as a fix and flip, in the same development as the cottage flip and on the same floor plan. The upstairs is a solid flip tour on its own. The Short is the basement, because of what Mike says at 18:37: they bought it to fix and sell, and the people buying it then asked them to finish the basement as well. So the best part of the house was never part of the job. The basement has a wet bar Mike calls one of the nicest they have ever done, an island on wheels, and a steam shower lined in slab that he says makes you feel like you are in the clouds. Finished basement footage runs 14:00 to 17:45, plus the sign off at the bar from 18:50 to 19:28, which is usable at left and right crops where Mike is out of frame.

avoid_ranges.reason: the garage. Good footage but a different Short

project_context.summary: A fix and flip the buyers bought mid project, then asked King to finish the basement too. The basement has a wet bar in stained wood with glass front uppers, under cabinet lighting, a stacked stone backsplash, a wine cooler and a heavily veined granite top, and the island in front of it rolls so it can be pushed out of the way. Behind the bar sits his office with custom built furniture and a linear fireplace, then the family room, then built ins at the foot of the stairs. The basement bathroom has a vessel sink on a green veined counter and a steam shower lined in slab with a bench, a niche and a digital control outside the glass.
project_context.segment_choice: One Short, cut from 14:19 to 16:34 plus two right hand crops of the sign off at 19:06 and 19:14. Nothing from the upstairs tour and nothing from the garage.
notes: The hook is that the basement was never part of the job. Mike says it at 18:37.

The upstairs has a Short of its own in it: they kept the kitchen boxes and replaced only the doors and drawer faces, then painted, and the master vanity has a drawer at the bottom where a top drawer cannot go. Left out of this one for room.
The family keep a large collection on open shelves down here. Frame the cabinetry and the room, not the collection.

shot_notes: Mike works the centre of the bar through the whole basement segment, so the clean windows are left and right crops. The ones found by scanning: the bar wide at 14:19 to 14:31, the bar sink and glassware at 14:31 to 14:39 held left, the office at 14:49 to 14:55 held left, the family room at 15:08 to 15:13 held left, the built ins at 15:34 to 15:38, the vessel sink at 16:00 to 16:05, the steam shower at 16:12 to 16:34, and the sign off at the bar at 19:00 to 19:22, which is clean at crop 0.22 and at 0.76 either side of him.

shorts.full_vo:
We bought this house to flip it, and the basement was not part of the plan. Then the people buying it asked us to finish it too. This is one of the nicest wet bars we have ever built.

And the island rolls. You can push it right out of the way. Wine cooler, under cabinet lights, and a counter I keep staring at. His office sits right behind it, with the furniture built to fit.

Then the family room, lit the way I light everything, because nobody wants a dark room. Built ins at the foot of the stairs. The bathroom down here has a vessel sink, with green running right through the stone.

And then there is this. A steam shower. Slab walls, a bench inside, and a niche for everything. All of that in a basement that was never on the list.
shorts.voice_direction: Warm and unhurried, a contractor who is quietly pleased that the part nobody asked for turned out to be the best part of the house.
